title: Guided batching & caching configuration — recommendation cards + guardrails
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: customers are uncertain which batching and caching settings to pick for different workloads. Current console exposes low-level knobs (batch size, batching window, KV cache TTL, prefix caching) but lacks context: when to prefer aggressive caching vs low-latency single-shot inference, how cost changes, and what risks (staleness, hallucination drift) are implied.

Goal: design a guided configuration surface on the Redwood Console Model Settings page that surfaces: (1) workload-driven recommendation cards, (2) quick simulation/preview of cost & latency impact, (3) lightweight guardrails with explainers and undo paths, and (4) a compact advanced view for power users. Deliver a Figma prototype, copy for explainers, and a design handoff with component specs and acceptance criteria for PM and ENG to implement.

Primary user stories:
- As a PM integrating generation endpoints, I want simple presets so I can pick a safe config without deep infra knowledge.
- As an ML engineer, I want to tune caching TTL and batching logic while seeing cost/latency tradeoffs.
- As an operator, I want automated guardrails that prevent config combos that violate latency SLOs or data freshness SLAs.
acceptance_criteria:
- Prototype screens for Recommendation cards, Config preview, Guardrail warnings, Confirm/Apply modal exist in Figma and linked.
- Each recommendation shows expected latency, estimated per-1M-token cost delta, and confidence band/conditions.
- UI enforces at least one safety guard: disallow KV cache TTL > X for sensitive models unless override acknowledged.
- A/B rollout plan documented: gradual enablement with telemetry events.
- Accessibility: all controls keyboard-focusable and labeled for screen readers.
- Handoff includes tokens-to-cost mapping, example metrics, and mock telemetry events for ENG.
design_notes:
High-level approach: present a row of 3 recommendation cards (Balanced, Cost-Optimized, Low-Latency). Each card includes: short summary, expected impact (latency % change), example workload signals (chat with long context, embeddings-heavy, high throughput), and an expandable section for 'why this recommendation'.

Recommendation details: cards are derived from heuristics + runtime metrics (we'll surface the top contributing signal). Show a simulated baseline vs recommended config in a small sparkline and a numeric cost delta per 1M tokens. Use color and icons: green = cost-save, blue = balanced, orange = latency-optimized.

Guardrails and explainers: non-blocking warnings for risky combos, blocking confirmations for changes that increase TTL beyond privacy thresholds, and an admin-only toggle to allow aggressive cache overrides. Provide an 'impact simulator' that samples recent requests to estimate hit-rate changes.

Advanced view: inline controls for batch size, batching window, max tokens per batch, KV cache TTL, prefix caching toggle, and a per-route override list. Default collapsed to avoid overwhelming new users.

Trade-offs considered: exposing exact cost numbers requires access to tokenization and pricing data; we use an estimated-per-1M token model for prototypes. Too many recommendations could confuse users; we settled on three main cards with 'customize' to reveal advanced knobs. We debated auto-apply vs preview-only; final decision: always preview first, require explicit apply to change live config.
decisions: Show three high-level recommendation cards: Balanced, Cost-Optimized, Low-Latency
Preview-only flow by default; explicit Apply required
Blocking confirmation required for cache TTL > 30 days on models flagged sensitive
Provide simulated cost delta per 1M tokens (estimate) rather than precise billing numbers for MVP

Finalize copy with Legal for guardrail language around data freshness and privacy

implementation_notes:
- Telemetry events to emit: recommendation_impression, recommendation_select, config_preview, config_apply, guardrail_override.
- Use estimated_cost_per_1M_token = configurable param from pricing service.
- Guardrail thresholds are feature-flagged per org, defaults: TTL_block_threshold = 30 days, batching_window_max_ms = 2000.
- Accessibility: ensure ARIA labels on recommendation cards and that expand/collapse state is conveyed to screen readers.
risks: Users may over-rely on recommendations and bypass advanced testing — mitigate with explicit preview and simulation
Estimated cost numbers may diverge from billing — label as estimated and link to pricing page
Sampling-based hit-rate estimator can mislead if traffic patterns change rapidly — include confidence bands and last-sampled timestamp
